summary.one_liner: Jaeger is an open-source distributed tracing platform, created by Uber and hosted by the CNCF, for collecting, storing, and viewing traces from instrumented applications.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Jaeger as a distributed tracing system with a UI, collector, query service, and pluggable storage backends. Applications instrumented with the OpenTelemetry SDK send traces over OTLP (gRPC on port 4317, HTTP on 4318), and the collector writes them to storage. The Jaeger UI reads from the query service to display traces. The quick start runs an all-in-one image with in-memory storage. The README also documents a version compatibility policy for deprecated configuration options, a Go version support policy, and a storage backend version support policy covering Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Cassandra, and ClickHouse. Build, contribution, and roadmap details are delegated to external documents.
use_cases: store traces in Elasticsearch, Cassandra, or ClickHouse
quick local trace testing with Docker
notable: All-in-one Docker image bundling UI, collector, query, and in-memory storage
Accepts traces via OTLP over gRPC and HTTP
Pluggable storage backends via gRPC storage plugin
Documented deprecation grace period of at least 3 months or two minor versions
caveats: The quick start uses in-memory storage, and the README points to the Getting Started Guide for production deployments
Storage backend versions outside the documented support policy are best-effort only
Build from source and contribution details are in external CONTRIBUTING document
